sources.entry: Stringer - Work-in-progress self-hosted, anti-social RSS reader. MIT Ruby

summary.one_liner: Stringer is a self-hosted RSS reader built on Rails and PostgreSQL that aims to be simple, with no social sharing, recommendations, or machine learning features.
summary.what_it_does: Stringer is a Ruby on Rails web app that uses PostgreSQL for storage, Hotwire (Turbo and Stimulus) for the front end, and GoodJob for background jobs. It supports keyboard shortcuts, with the shortcut list opened by pressing `?`. It exposes a clone of Fever's API so mobile clients that support Fever can read feeds from it. It can run under a custom domain via CNAME on Heroku. A rake task, `cleanup_old_stories`, removes read, unstarred stories older than 30 days by default and can be run manually or on a schedule. The interface language is set with the LOCALE environment variable.
use_cases: read feeds on a mobile app via Fever API
deploy a personal news reader to Heroku
run an RSS reader in Docker
keep a private feed reader with no social features
clean up old read articles automatically
how_to_run: Install the toolchain versions pinned in .tool-versions (Ruby, Node, PostgreSQL, pnpm)
Run bin/setup to install dependencies, prepare the database, and launch the dev server on port 3000
Start the server later with bin/dev
Run tests with bundle exec rspec
notable: Fever API clone, so existing Fever-compatible mobile clients work with it
Runs on Heroku Eco/Basic plans, per the README
Deployment instructions for Heroku, generic Linux VPS, Docker, and OpenShift
caveats: Described by its own listing as work-in-progress
Development setup requires specific pinned toolchain versions (Ruby, Node, PostgreSQL, pnpm)
Heroku custom domain setup requires editing DNS records at your registrar
